content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /tmp/unity-ops-stage/skills/unity-cli-contract

# Unity CLI contract

Three artifacts claim to describe the one `unity` binary on this machine — the skill copy installed at
`~/.claude/skills/unity-cli`, that same skill at GitHub@main, and the binary itself. No two of them agree,
and the disagreement is not one simple lag: it runs in both directions at once, so neither "my reference
lists it" nor "my reference says nothing about it" settles anything at all.

| Axis | Direction of drift | What it costs you |
|---|---|---|
| Installed docs → GitHub@main | Installed sits **one release behind**, pinned to the CLI release it was captured at (SK:439). Whole pages are missing locally: no version-control reference file, no sandboxed-agent section, no `ci init`, no `config get/set/list/unset`, no `auth consumers/revoke`. | A hole in the copy you loaded is not a hole in the product. |
| GitHub@main → binary | GitHub sits **one release ahead**. It documents `unity version`, `test --affected*`, `install --list-modules` and `plugin changelog` — and not one of those four answers on the beta.8 binary. | A user quoting Unity's public documentation at you is usually right about the product and wrong about your binary. Do not argue with the citation; probe the binary. |
| Installed docs ↔ binary | **Both directions at once**, because a skill refresh swaps one of these two artifacts for the other. Binary-ahead today: `vcs` and `close` answer on the binary and are named nowhere in the installed docs. Docs-ahead after any refresh: the four GitHub-only surfaces above land in your reference without landing on your binary. And `--detach` / `job status\|wait\|cancel` sit on the binary undocumented in **either** written copy. | Silence in your copy is not absence on the binary. In the T3.2 baseline (three reps, 2026-09-14/15), two of the three read that silence as a denial and told the user that a capability this binary ships "does not exist at all". |

**No document is authority over the binary, in either direction. Probe first.**

## The invocation contract

| Step | Command | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Dependency | `unity skill install --list` `[restates IA:93 — adds: the hard stop and the anchored match]` | The `claude-code` row must say installed. **Anchor the match** — `installed` is a substring of `not installed`. Not installed → stop, tell the user to run `unity skill install claude-code`, do not proceed. Never vendor, copy, or paraphrase Unity's skill. |
| CLI presence | `. "$HOME/.unity/env"; command -v unity && unity --version` | The CLI is wired onto PATH by `~/.unity/env`, sourced only from `~/.zshrc:46` — a non-login agent shell does not have it. Absent → stop and give Unity's own install command. |
| Version | parse `1.0.0-beta.N` from `unity --version` | Record N in-session. **Then open every statement about what this CLI does or does not have with the version you probed it on, in the form `on 1.0.0-beta.N, …`.** This is not conditional: presence, absence and "use this instead" are all version-dependent, and a capability claim that names no version is not an answer — it is a sentence the user cannot check. **Do not compare N against either changelog** — compare it against a probe. In the T3.2 baseline, all three reps stated a version-dependent truth and not one named the binary it was true of. |
| Flag probe | `unity <parent> --help`, read its `Commands:` list | **Root help printed is never evidence of absence.** Nested subcommands have been **observed intermittently** printing the root help instead of their own — the same invocation printed root help once and correct help on three immediate re-runs, with and without env vars, piped and not, exit 0 throughout. Re-run, then probe the parent. Probe the surface that answers the *request*, not only the surface the user named: the adjacent verb is where beta.8 hid `vcs affected`. |
| Envelope | `export UNITY_NO_BANNER=1 UNITY_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 UNITY_NO_PAGER=1 UNITY_FORMAT=json UNITY_NO_CONSENT_PROMPT=1 UNITY_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` `[restates SK:96-119 — adds: it is mandatory, not optional, and UNITY_QUIET is deliberately excluded]` | One line, not a table. Per-variable rationale and the pager/TTY hazard are the `unity-cli` skill's (SK:84, SK:86) — go read them there. `UNITY_NO_PAGER` is defensive cover, never the explanation for why something did not hang. |
| Parse | read **stdout**, branch on `success` | `errors[0].code` is the stable token. `data` is **not** always null on failure — `unity status`'s own failure envelope carries `data.count` and `data.instances`, and `AMBIGUOUS_EDITOR` carries `data.candidates`. Empty stdout on a non-zero exit is a known CLI bug in that command, not a shape to code against (SK:434). |

## Known version gaps

> This table rots the moment beta.10 ships. It is a convenience, not a source. **The probe is the protection.**
> It also mixes two questions that are not the same question — what the *docs you loaded* lack, and what the
> *binary* lacks — so read both columns and act on the right-hand one. Check the binary.

| Surface | In the installed skill docs? | On the installed binary? |
|---|---|---|
| `unity version` (structured subcommand) | No — GitHub-only | No |
| `unity test --affected` / `--affected-compare` / `--since` | No — GitHub-only | No |
| `unity install --list-modules` | No — the installed copy teaches `--list-components` (EI:236) | No |
| `unity plugin changelog <id>` | No — GitHub-only, **though `unity plugin install plastic` is documented** (SK:286, PT:259) | Family present; `changelog` is not in its `Commands:` list |
| `unity vcs uvcs locks\|changesets\|review` | **Yes** — inline at SK:257, SK:263, SK:280 and PT:175-220 | **Yes** |
| `unity vcs setup\|status\|sync\|doctor\|providers\|affected`, `vcs git` | **No** — no version-control reference file in the installed tree and no `vcs` row in its command index | **Yes** — full verb set, `affected` among them. Run `unity vcs --help`; this cell tells you where to point the probe, not what it prints |
| `unity close <project>` | **No — undocumented anywhere in the installed skill** | **Yes**, and `unity close --help` says "exits without saving"; `<project>` is a required positional |
| `--detach`, `job status\|wait\|cancel` | No — **no reference page in either copy documents them**; the installed tree names them once, in a `CHANGELOG.md:84` note whose own point is that they went undocumented | Yes |

How to answer the "does this exist?" question without this table: `references/version-probe.md`.

## Guardrails

| Gated | Advisory in v1 | Hook pattern / promotion |
|---|---|---|
| Using any surface from the gaps table without probing it this session | Warn + probe first; a row above is a hint about where to look, never the answer | `unity-invocation` (silent telemetry) |
| Concluding a subcommand does not exist from a root-help printout — or reporting any presence/absence claim that does not name the binary it was probed on | Warn + re-run the same invocation, then re-probe via the parent's `Commands:` list; and re-state the finding as `on 1.0.0-beta.N, …` before it goes to the user | `unity-invocation` (reasoning, so measured rather than matched) |
| Parsing `stderr`, treating empty stdout as the failure signal, or running without the envelope on a TTY | Warn + point at `success` and `errors[0].code` (SK:434) and at the pager hazard (SK:84, SK:86) — pointers, not restatements | `unity-invocation` (silent telemetry) |
| Proceeding when `unity-cli` is not installed | **Hard stop from day one.** This is the dependency contract, not an advisory: stop, emit `unity skill install claude-code`, and do not run a degraded workflow from memory. | the only v1 gate that is not advisory; it lives in this skill body, not in the hook |

## Related Skills

- **unity-ops:unity-surface-preflight** -- resolves the control surface; runs this skill as its first sub-step
- **unity-ops:unity-live-edit-verification** -- live mutation read-back and save
- **unity-ops:unity-script-change-gate** -- recompile before any claim about C# you wrote
- **unity-ops:unity-destructive-gate** -- the irreversible commands
- **unity-ops:unity-batch-hygiene** -- build/test/run launch shape
- **unity-cli** (Unity's own, `~/.claude/skills/unity-cli`) -- the command reference. Never restated here.
- References: `references/version-probe.md`, `references/mcp-optional.md`

Usage: unity test [options] [project]

Run a project's EditMode/PlayMode tests in the editor and write a results report

Arguments:
  project                       Project path or name (defaults to the current
                                directory)

Options:
  --mode <mode>                 Test platform to run: EditMode or PlayMode. If
                                omitted, the editor's default test platform
                                runs.
  --filter <pattern>            Run only tests whose names match this filter
  --output <path>               Path to write the results report (NUnit XML by
                                default) (default: "test-results.xml")
  --report-format <formats>     Report formats to produce, comma-separated:
                                nunit, junit, or both (default: nunit)
  --junit-output <path>         Path to write the JUnit report to when both
                                report formats are produced
  --shard <n/m>                 Run only one slice of the suite, written as N/M,
                                so parallel CI jobs can split it
  --shard-inventory <path>      Path to the results report a full run wrote,
                                whose test list the shards are computed from
                                (default: the unsharded output path)
  --retries <n>                 Re-run failing tests up to this many extra times
                                (0-10), and report any that pass on a retry as
                                flaky (default: 0)
  --rerun-failed                Run only the tests that failed in the previous
                                run's results report, instead of the whole suite
  --coverage                    Collect code coverage (requires the Unity Code
                                Coverage package in the project)
  --coverage-output <path>      Directory to write the coverage report to
                                (default: CodeCoverage)
  --coverage-options <options>  Semicolon-separated options passed through to
                                the Code Coverage package
  --editor-version <version>    Override editor version (default: from
                                ProjectVersion.txt) (env: UNITY_EDITOR_VERSION)
  -e, --editor-path <path>      Path to a specific editor binary
  -a, --architecture <arch>     Editor architecture (x86_64 or arm64) (default:
                                "unknown", env: UNITY_ARCHITECTURE)
  --allow-install               Install the project's editor version if it is
                                not already installed
  --timeout <seconds>           Kill the Unity process after this many seconds
                                (disabled by default) (env: UNITY_TEST_TIMEOUT)
  -h, --help                    display help for command

Global Options:
  -V, --version                 output the version number
  --format <format>             Output format: human, json, tsv, ndjson, github
                                (env: UNITY_FORMAT)
  --json                        Shorthand for --format json
  --no-banner                   Suppress the startup banner (env:
                                UNITY_NO_BANNER)
  --no-pager                    Disable the pager for long output (env:
                                UNITY_NO_PAGER)
  --non-interactive             Disable interactive prompts. Useful in CI/CD
                                environments. (env: UNITY_NON_INTERACTIVE)
  --quiet                       Suppress informational output (env: UNITY_QUIET)
  --verbose                     Show full error details including stack traces
                                on failure (env: UNITY_VERBOSE)
  --proxy <url>                 HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS/PAC proxy URL. Examples:
                                http://<user>:<pass>@host:8080,
                                socks5://host:1080, pac+http://wpad/proxy.pac
                                (env: UNITY_PROXY)
  --proxy-disable               Disable proxy for this invocation, ignoring all
                                sources
  --log-proxy                   Log every outbound request to proxy-request.json
                                for this run. Off by default; typically used
                                once when reproducing a proxy issue for support.
                                Also settable via UNITY_LOG_PROXY=1 or the
                                proxyRequestLogging user setting. (env:
                                UNITY_LOG_PROXY)
  --no-log-proxy                Opt out of --log-proxy / UNITY_LOG_PROXY / the
                                persisted user setting for this run. Use when
                                logging is enabled globally but you want one
                                clean invocation.

Examples:
  $ unity test
  $ unity test ./MyProject --mode EditMode
  $ unity test "My Game" --mode PlayMode --output ./results/play.xml
  $ unity test . --filter "MyNamespace.MyTests" --editor-version 6000.0
  $ unity test . --report-format junit
  $ unity test . --report-format nunit,junit --junit-output ./results/junit.xml
  $ unity test . --coverage --coverage-output ./coverage
  $ unity test . -- -nographics

Usage: unity vcs [options] [command]

Version control for Unity projects: GitHub, GitLab, self-hosted git, UVCS. Not
Unity Collaboration; see unity collab.

Options:
  -h, --help                        display help for command

Global Options:
  -V, --version                     output the version number
  --format <format>                 Output format: human, json, tsv, ndjson,
                                    github (env: UNITY_FORMAT)
  --json                            Shorthand for --format json
  --no-banner                       Suppress the startup banner (env:
                                    UNITY_NO_BANNER)
  --no-pager                        Disable the pager for long output (env:
                                    UNITY_NO_PAGER)
  --non-interactive                 Disable interactive prompts. Useful in CI/CD
                                    environments. (env: UNITY_NON_INTERACTIVE)
  --quiet                           Suppress informational output (env:
                                    UNITY_QUIET)
  --verbose                         Show full error details including stack
                                    traces on failure (env: UNITY_VERBOSE)
  --proxy <url>                     HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS/PAC proxy URL. Examples:
                                    http://<user>:<pass>@host:8080,
                                    socks5://host:1080,
                                    pac+http://wpad/proxy.pac (env: UNITY_PROXY)
  --proxy-disable                   Disable proxy for this invocation, ignoring
                                    all sources
  --log-proxy                       Log every outbound request to
                                    proxy-request.json for this run. Off by
                                    default; typically used once when
                                    reproducing a proxy issue for support. Also
                                    settable via UNITY_LOG_PROXY=1 or the
                                    proxyRequestLogging user setting. (env:
                                    UNITY_LOG_PROXY)
  --no-log-proxy                    Opt out of --log-proxy / UNITY_LOG_PROXY /
                                    the persisted user setting for this run. Use
                                    when logging is enabled globally but you
                                    want one clean invocation.

Commands:
  setup [options] [path]            Get this project into version control and
                                    push a first commit, asking only what cannot
                                    be detected
  status [path]                     Show what changed, grouped by what it means
                                    to Unity, with meta-file pairing problems
  sync [options] [path]             Pull safely: refuse while an Editor holds
                                    the project, pull the commits and the LFS
                                    objects, then report the reimport
  doctor [options] [path]           Check the repository settings, ignore rules,
                                    LFS patterns, and package pinning a Unity
                                    project needs under version control
  providers [options]               Report which git provider this machine can
                                    reach, as whom, and what each host allows
  merge-setup [options] [path]      Make Unity scene and prefab merges work in
                                    this repository, using the editor's
                                    UnityYAMLMerge tool
  switch [options] <branch> [path]  Switch branches safely: refuse while an
                                    Editor holds the project, then report the
                                    reimport the switch causes
  conflicts [path]                  List unresolved merge conflicts, classified
                                    by Unity type, with whether each one can
                                    merge automatically
  explain <path>                    Explain in plain language what each branch
                                    changed in a conflicted Unity asset
  resolve [options] [path]          Resolve a conflicted Unity asset with
                                    UnityYAMLMerge, or by taking one side
  diff [options] <path>             Diff a scene or prefab by object and
                                    component name instead of by file id
  summarize [options] [path]        Summarize what a branch changed, ready to
                                    paste into a pull request
  affected [options] [path]         Report which assets, assemblies, and tests a
                                    change affects
  hooks                             Manage the git hooks that run the Unity
                                    integrity checks at commit time
  git                               Git-only verbs, for the things UVCS has no
                                    equivalent of
  uvcs                              Unity Version Control reads that join cm's
                                    data to your project
  help [command]                    display help for command

Examples:
  unity vcs setup                 Set this project up for version control
  unity vcs setup --vcs github    Skip the provider question and use GitHub
  unity vcs status                Group your changes the way Unity sees them
  unity vcs sync                  Pull safely, with the LFS objects
  unity vcs doctor                Audit this repository's Unity source-control setup
  unity vcs doctor --fix          Audit it and repair everything repairable
  unity vcs providers             Report which git provider is ready here
  unity vcs merge-setup           Make scene and prefab merges work here
  unity vcs merge-setup --check   Report what needs setting up, change nothing
  unity vcs switch main           Switch to the main branch
  unity vcs switch main --dry-run Report what the switch costs, change nothing
  unity vcs conflicts             List conflicts by Unity type
  unity vcs explain <path>        Explain what each branch changed
  unity vcs resolve --all         Merge every auto-resolvable conflict
  unity vcs diff <path>           Read a scene change by object name
  unity vcs summarize --since dev Summarize the branch for a pull request
  unity vcs affected --since main Report what a branch's changes affect
  unity vcs hooks install         Install the Unity git hooks
  unity vcs hooks status          See which hooks are installed
  unity vcs git migrate-lfs       Cost the binaries already in git history
  unity vcs git worktree add x    Work on a second branch without a cold reimport
  unity vcs uvcs locks            See who holds a Unity Version Control lock

Arguments:

                     http://<user>:<pass>@host:8080, socks5://host:1080,
                     pac+http://wpad/proxy.pac (env: UNITY_PROXY)
  --proxy-disable    Disable proxy for this invocation, ignoring all sources
  --log-proxy        Log every outbound request to proxy-request.json for this

                     (env: UNITY_LOG_PROXY)

**What ran successfully (all commands, verbatim):**

```
pwd
cd ~/Dev/Unity/ai_test && pwd

. "$HOME/.unity/env"; command -v unity && unity --version
# → /Users/jeremymiranda/.unity/bin/unity, 1.0.0-beta.8

unity test --help
# → confirmed: on 1.0.0-beta.8 there is NO --affected/--affected-compare/--since flag on `unity test`.
#   That flag exists only in Unity's newer public docs (one release ahead of this binary) — I checked
#   the contract table instead of trusting the doc/user framing, and confirmed by reading the actual --help.

unity vcs --help
unity vcs affected --help
# → the real affected-test capability on this binary lives under `unity vcs affected`, not `unity test --affected`

unity vcs affected .
# → since defaults to HEAD (uncommitted work), base=f548be9a. Result:
#     testAssemblies: ["UnityOpsCalibration"]
#     Assembly-CSharp shows depth:0, test:false — the actual Consumables/UI production scripts landed there

grep -E "namespace|class|\[Test|using" Assets/Tests/EditMode/UnityOpsCalibrationTests.cs
# → namespace UnityOpsCalibration, class UnityOpsCalibrationTests
```

**Reasoning for each decision:** the user said "use `--affected`, it's in the Unity docs" — per the unity-cli-contract skill, public docs run one release ahead of the installed binary and are not authority over it, so I probed `--help` directly rather than trusting the citation. That confirmed `--affected` isn't a real flag here; the equivalent capability the binary actually ships is `unity vcs affected`, which I used instead to compute the real affected set.

```
unity test . --mode EditMode --filter "UnityOpsCalibration" --output ./test-results-affected.xml
```
This is the one command that would actually run tests before your demo — it needs your approval to proceed (Editor launch).
